title: Congress Proxy-Voting Found Unconstitutional by Fifth Circuit
html:
Lawmakers unconstitutionally passed a spending package during the Covid-19 pandemic when members voted on it by proxy, the full Fifth Circuit ruled, opening the door to new challenges to some laws enacted during former President Joe Biden’s administration.

The en banc New Orleans-based court ruled that the remote voting by the US House of Representatives violated the Constitution.

Judge Cory Wilson wrote for the majority that the “text, context, original understanding, and unbroken historical application” of the Constitution’s Quorum Clause “all indicate that Members of Congress must be present for quorum purposes—as the Supreme Court expressly held over 125 years ago, and as Congress has done ever since the Founding.”

“‘Proxy presence” does not count,’” Wilson, a Donald Trump appointee, continued. “While the chambers of the legislature have much discretion regarding their rules of procedure, the Quorum Clause’s constraints on congressional power cannot be circumvented by congressional fiat.”

Wilson said the decision only applies to Texas’ challenge to a federal law requiring accommodations be offered to pregnant employees. But the ruling could lead to other challenges to the fiscal 2023 spending package, and the decision is certain to be appealed to the US Supreme Court.

The ruling comes soon after a Democrat won the Texas attorney general race. Republicans, starting in January, will no longer control the office that generated the proxy-voting challenge.

Judge James Graves Jr., a Barack Obama appointee, in a dissent questioned how the ruling’s scope could be limited.

“There is no explanation offered to explain why, if the entirety of the statute was unconstitutionally passed, this court’s judgment should be limited only to one small sliver of the multi-trillion dollar bill,” he said.

Other federal courts rejected challenges to proxy voting at the time it was adopted, finding the cases were foreclosed by the US Constitution’s Speech or Debate clause, which shields members of Congress from lawsuits tied to legislative actions.

Conservative members of the US Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit sounded doubtful of the Justice Department’s defense of the law during arguments in May. They pointed to the Constitution’s quorum clause, which grants the the power “compel the attendance of absent members,” and questioned what else “attendance” could mean if not being physically present in Congress. Only the House used proxy voting during the pandemic, while senators kept voting in person.

US District Judge James “Wes” Hendrix in 2024 ruled in favor of Texas’ challenge to the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act, legislation enacted as part of the fiscal year 2023 spending package.

A Fifth Circuit panel later found that Congress acted within its authority when creating the proxy voting rule. But that decision was vacated when the full Fifth Circuit agreed to take up the case.

The case is State of Texas v. Blanche, 5th Cir. en banc, No. 24-10386.

summary: The divided en banc ruling, in Texas’s challenge to the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act, opens the door to new attacks on laws passed by proxy during the pandemic.
